trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Use morning for in-flight rest and preparation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Barcelona Airport at 13:00. Take the Aerobus (€5.90 one-way) or Metro L9 Sud (€5.15) to Eixample district. Check in to Barcelona Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation walk along Passeig de Gràcia to spot the iconic facades of Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) from the outside — free to admire exteriors.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Eixample neighborhood on foot. Head to Carrer del Consell de Cent or Carrer de Muntaner for a classic Barcelona aperitivo experience. Grab a seat at a local bar for vermouth (vermut) and free tapas pintxos. Stroll through the illuminated Eixample grid streets and soak in the Art Nouveau architecture lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick coffee and croissant at the airport — budget €3–5.
meals.lunch: Pick up a bocadillo (sandwich) or slice of pizza near the hotel from a local bakery or supermercado (Mercadona or Lidl nearby) — budget €4–6.
meals.dinner: Bar Calders or a local menú del día restaurant in Eixample offering a 3-course dinner with wine for €12–15. Look for chalkboard signs saying 'Menú Noche'.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€11.35) upon arrival — it will save money throughout the trip. August is hot in Barcelona (30°C+), so carry water and wear light clothing. Keep valuables secure on the Metro.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Sagrada Família (book tickets online in advance — €26 basic entry, or €20.50 for just the basilica). Arrive early (9:00–9:30) to beat the crowds. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring Gaudí's masterpiece. Afterward, walk through the surrounding Sant Martí neighborhood and admire the surrounding streets filled with Modernista buildings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take Metro to Park Güell (free to enter the monumental zone with pre-booked free timed ticket — book at parkguell.barcelona). Explore the iconic mosaic terraces, Gaudí's gingerbread gatehouses (€10 for monumental zone), and the free surrounding forested park with panoramic city views. Spend 2–3 hours here. Take Metro back to Eixample and rest during the hottest part of the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) after dinner — a 15-minute Metro ride from Eixample. Wander the narrow medieval streets, visit Plaça Reial (free), and check out the live music and street performers. This area comes alive after 21:00. If budget allows, peek into a flamenco bar or enjoy a €3 beer at a terrace bar in the square.

meals.breakfast: Café de l'Acadèmia or a local granja near the hotel — coffee and toast with tomato (pa amb tomàquet) for €3–5.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Park Güell — buy supplies from a nearby supermercado (bread, cheese, cured meats, fruit) for €6–8 total.
meals.dinner: Bar Marsella or a menú del día spot in the Gothic Quarter — 3-course meal with wine for €13–15. Try Bar Celta for cheap pulpo (octopus) tapas.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets at least 2–3 weeks in advance in August as they sell out. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Carry a reusable water bottle — public drinking fountains are available throughout the city.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the El Born / Sant Pere neighborhood. Visit the stunning Palau de la Música Catalana (exterior is free; guided tours from €22 — consider the cheaper self-guided audio option). Browse the surrounding streets filled with boutiques and street art. Walk to the nearby Mercat de Santa Caterina (free entry) — a colorful alternative to La Boqueria with fewer tourists and better local prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Barceloneta Beach (free) via Metro or a 20-minute walk from El Born. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing on the Mediterranean. Walk along the Passeig Marítim boardwalk and explore the Port Olímpic marina area. Visit the large Frank Gehry fish sculpture (El Peix) — free photo opportunity. Cool off with a €2 granizado (crushed ice drink) from a beach kiosk.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample for the famous 'Eixample Esquerra' LGBTQ+ nightlife scene (known as Gayxample) — vibrant bars and clubs along Carrer del Consell de Cent. Alternatively, visit Razzmatazz or Sala Apolo (entry €10–15 with a drink included) for live music or DJ sets. Barcelona nightlife starts late — clubs fill up after midnight.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café in El Born or similar — avocado toast and coffee for €7–9 (a slight splurge but worth it).
meals.lunch: Mercat de Santa Caterina food stalls — fresh tapas, grilled fish, or a bocadillo for €6–9.
meals.dinner: Pre-club dinner at a budget tapas bar in Eixample — patatas bravas, pan con tomate, and croquetas for €10–13 total. Try Cervecería Catalana for affordable classic tapas.

day_by_day.notes: Barceloneta can get extremely crowded in August. Arrive before 12:00 to secure a good spot. Keep bags attended on the beach. For nightlife, note that most clubs don't get busy until 1:00–2:00 AM — plan a late dinner and pre-drinks at a bar to save money.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Montjuïc (or the cable car for €12.70 return — budget option is bus 150 for €2.40 with T-Casual card). Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (€14 entry — check for free Sunday morning slots). Explore the Montjuïc Castle (€5 entry) with sweeping panoramic views over Barcelona and the port. Walk the castle ramparts and enjoy the breeze above the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Montjuïc and visit the Pavelló Mies van der Rohe — the iconic Barcelona Pavilion (€7 entry), a must-see for architecture lovers. A masterpiece of modernist rationalist design. Walk to nearby Plaça d'Espanya and admire the Venetian Towers and the MNAC (Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya) — enter the building's rooftop terrace for free city views even without buying a museum ticket (€12 if you want to see the collection). Stroll down Avinguda de la Reina Maria Cristina.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample and explore Gràcia neighborhood — take a short walk or Metro to this bohemian village-within-a-city. Wander through Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia, both packed with locals drinking and socializing on terrace bars. This is authentic Barcelona at its best. If visiting mid-August, check if the famous Festa Major de Gràcia street festival is on (usually Aug 15–21) — free street decorations, concerts, and festivities.

meals.breakfast: Grab coffee and a croissant at a local café near the hotel for €3–4. Or visit a Forn de Pa (bakery) for fresh pastries.
meals.lunch: Picnic on Montjuïc with supermarket supplies, or eat at the affordable café inside the Fundació Joan Miró — menú del día for €12.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Gràcia neighborhood — La Pepita or a local pizzeria/tapas bar with outdoor seating for €10–14. Try a glass of local cava (sparkling wine) for €2–3.

day_by_day.notes: Check the Montjuïc Magic Fountain show schedule (free light and music show, usually Thursday–Sunday evenings in summer at 21:30–22:30) — if available, this is a spectacular free evening activity. Confirm 2027 schedule locally upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning walk along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the 'Block of Discord' (Manzana de la Discòrdia) — three competing Modernista buildings: Casa Lleó Morera, Casa Amatller, and Casa Batlló, all within one city block. Admire exteriors for free. Visit the interior of Casa Amatller (€19) or Casa Batlló (€35 — splurge option) if budget allows. Pop into any remaining Eixample streets you haven't explored and photograph the distinctive octagonal street corners (xamfrans) unique to Cerdà's urban grid.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit El Raval neighborhood — explore the MACBA (Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona) exterior plaza, a popular skateboarding spot and architectural landmark (free to enjoy outside; €12 for entry). Walk to the nearby CCCB cultural center (free courtyard). Browse the Mercat de Sant Antoni — a beautifully restored 19th-century iron market with a popular Sunday book market (check if open). Head back to the hotel to pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Final farewell dinner in Eixample. Splurge slightly on a sit-down meal at a traditional Catalan restaurant — try escalivada, fideuà (noodle paella), or crema catalana for dessert. Budget €18–22 for a full meal. If departing late, enjoy one last vermouth at a rooftop bar or terrace in the Eixample before heading to the airport.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a proper Spanish breakfast — café con leche, fresh orange juice, and toast with tomato and jamón at a local café for €6–8.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a bocadillo shop or supermercado to keep costs down before the final dinner splurge — €5–7.
meals.dinner: Farewell Catalan dinner at a mid-range local restaurant in Eixample — Restaurant Parking Pizza or similar well-reviewed local spot for €18–22 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed (most hotels offer this for free). Allow at least 90 minutes to reach the airport from Eixample via Aerobus or Metro L9. Barcelona Airport is very busy in August — arrive 2.5 hours before departure. Keep your T-Casual metro card for the airport journey if trips remain.

trip_options.title: Classic Barcelona Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.description: Explore Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica with a skip-the-line guided tour. Marvel at the intricate facades, stunning stained glass interiors, and climb the towers for panoramic city views. A must-see masterpiece of modernist architecture.

experiences.name: Nightlife Experience on Passeig del Born & Barceloneta Club Strip
experiences.description: Experience Barcelona's legendary nightlife starting with craft cocktails at rooftop bars in El Born, then head to the Barceloneta beach club strip for world-class DJ sets at iconic open-air clubs. Barcelona nightlife peaks after midnight and runs until dawn.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In — Flight lands at 13:00, so the morning slot is travel time. Take the Aerobus or Metro L9 from El Prat Airport to Eixample (~35 min). Check in to Barcelona Boutique Stay, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Eixample Architecture Walk — Stroll the famous 'Manzana de la Discordia' (Block of Discord) on Passeig de Gràcia, just steps from the hotel. Admire the exteriors of Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera. If energy allows, purchase a timed entry to Casa Batlló (~€35) for a self-guided interior tour. This is a perfect low-key introduction to Modernisme without over-scheduling after a flight.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner & First Night Out in Eixample — Head to a classic Catalan restaurant like Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca for dinner. Afterward, explore the 'Gayxample' bar scene along Carrer del Consell de Cent for relaxed cocktails and a gentle taste of Barcelona's nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or on arrival — skip a full breakfast given the midday landing.
meals.lunch: Quick bite near the hotel: Bar Calders in Sant Antoni (10-min walk) for a bocadillo and fresh juice (~€10–12).
meals.dinner: Cervecería Catalana — tapas and Catalan classics, mid-range (~€20–28 per person). Arrive before 21:00 to avoid long queues.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light to recover from travel. Keep luggage at the hotel's storage if check-in isn't ready before 15:00. August in Barcelona is hot (28–32°C expected) — carry water and wear light clothing.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — Book the skip-the-line guided tour (9:00 or 10:00 slot recommended; ~€35–45 with towers). The basilica is a 15-minute walk or short Metro ride (L2/L5 to Sagrada Família) from Eixample. Spend 2–2.5 hours exploring the Nativity and Passion facades, the awe-inspiring nave, and the museum crypt.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration — Take Bus 24 or a taxi up to Park Güell (~€10 timed entry for the Monumental Zone; book in advance). Spend 1.5 hours among the mosaic terraces, Dragon Staircase, and panoramic city views. Descend into the charming Gràcia neighborhood for a leisurely wander through Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Gràcia & Rooftop Drinks — Dine in Gràcia before heading back. Afterward, return to Eixample and visit the rooftop bar at Hotel Pulitzer or the Terraza del Claris for sundowner cocktails with skyline views (~€12–16 per cocktail).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby: Federal Café on Carrer del Parlament (~€10–14) — excellent eggs and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic supplies from Mercat de l'Abaceria in Gràcia, or a set lunch menu (menú del día) at a Gràcia local restaurant (~€13–15 for 3 courses with wine).
meals.dinner: La Pepita in Gràcia — creative montaditos and tapas, vibrant atmosphere (~€18–25 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online at least 2–3 weeks in advance — both sell out quickly in August. Wear comfortable walking shoes; Park Güell involves uphill paths. The Monumental Zone at Park Güell has a daily visitor cap.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour — Join a guided Gothic Quarter walking tour (departing ~10:00 from Plaça Nova; ~€15–20 for a small group tour). Discover Roman walls, the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and hidden medieval alleyways. The tour typically lasts 2–2.5 hours and provides rich historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tapas & Vermouth Food Tour in El Born — Transition directly from the Gothic Quarter into the adjacent El Born district for the guided tapas and vermouth food tour (~14:00 start; ~€65–75 per person including food and drinks). Visit 4–5 stops sampling pintxos, jamón, anchovies, and house vermouth. Finish near the stunning Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar.
day_by_day.evening: Nightlife Experience on Passeig del Born & Barceloneta Club Strip — Begin the evening with craft cocktails at a rooftop bar in El Born (Bar del Pla or El Xampanyet for cava). Around 23:00, walk or take a short cab to Barceloneta beach clubs (Opium, Pacha, or Shoko) for Barcelona's legendary late-night scene. Clubs peak after midnight.

meals.breakfast: Forn de Sant Jaume bakery on Rambla de Catalunya — fresh pastries and café amb llet (~€6–8).
meals.lunch: Covered by the El Born food tour (included in the experience price).
meals.dinner: Light pre-club dinner: Bar del Pla in El Born — excellent patatas bravas, croquetas, and grilled vegetables (~€15–20 per person).

day_by_day.notes: This is the most activity-dense day, combining two guided experiences. Wear comfortable shoes for the morning walking tour. For the nightlife portion, note that Barcelona clubs have a cover charge of ~€15–20 (often includes one drink). Taxis back to Eixample from Barceloneta cost ~€10–12. Consider a later checkout the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery Morning & Modernisme Deep Dive — After the late night, start slow. Visit Casa Milà (La Pedrera) at a relaxed 10:30 or 11:00 entry (~€28). The rooftop with its warrior chimney warriors is extraordinary, and the Espai Gaudí exhibition in the attic is world-class. La Pedrera is a 5-minute walk from the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montjuïc Hill Exploration — Take the Metro to Paral·lel and ride the Funicular de Montjuïc up to the hill. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (~€14) for a dose of modern art, then walk to the Castell de Montjuïc for sweeping harbor views. Explore the 1929 Exposition Pavilion (Mies van der Rohe Pavilion, ~€12) — a must for architecture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Bunkers del Carmel & El Born Dinner — Take a taxi or Bus V17 to the Bunkers del Carmel (Turó de la Rovira) for the best 360° panoramic sunset view of Barcelona (~19:30–20:30 in August). Free entry. Afterward, head to El Born for a relaxed dinner and final evening stroll along the illuminated Passeig del Born.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at Cosmo on Carrer d'Enric Granados — avocado toast, smoothies, relaxed atmosphere (~€12–16). Open from 10:00.
meals.lunch: Bodega Sepúlveda near Montjuïc — traditional Catalan tavern with a menú del día (~€13–15).
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet in El Born — legendary local bar with house cava and traditional tapas (~€18–22 per person). Go early (~20:30) as it fills fast.

day_by_day.notes: La Pedrera tickets should be booked in advance online. The Bunkers del Carmel is a local favorite for sunset — bring a light layer as the hilltop breeze can be cool after dark. August sunsets are around 20:45–21:00, so time the Bunkers visit accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Sant Antoni Market & Eixample Farewell Walk — Visit the beautifully restored Mercat de Sant Antoni (10-min walk from hotel) for a final morning browse of fresh produce, local cheeses, and artisan goods. Pick up souvenirs and provisions. Then take a final architectural stroll down Enric Granados boulevard — a pedestrian-friendly Modernisme showcase lined with café terraces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Barceloneta Beach & Port Olímpic — Head to Barceloneta beach for a few relaxed hours of sun and sea (Metro L4 to Barceloneta). Walk along the Passeig Marítim, visit the iconic Frank Gehry gold fish sculpture at Port Olímpic, and enjoy a final afternoon by the Mediterranean. Return to the hotel by 17:00 to pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner in Eixample — End the trip with a special dinner at Parking Pizza on Londres Street (beloved local favorite, ~€15–20) or splurge slightly at Bodega Sepúlveda for Catalan classics. Toast the trip with a glass of cava before heading to the airport or retiring early.

meals.breakfast: Sant Antoni Market — fresh fruit, artisan bread, and a coffee from one of the market bars (~€6–8).
meals.lunch: La Cova Fumada in Barceloneta (cash only, arrive early — closes by 15:00) — legendary local spot, birthplace of the bombas tapa (~€15–20 per person).
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza on Carrer de Londres — wood-fired Neapolitan pizzas in a buzzing Eixample setting (~€16–22 per person). Great for a relaxed final night.

day_by_day.notes: If departing on Day 5 evening, confirm hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed. La Cova Fumada is cash only and closes early — plan accordingly. Consider buying a bottle of local cava or Catalan wine from a Vilaviniteca shop as a take-home gift. The Aerobus from Passeig de Gràcia to El Prat takes ~35 minutes.

Pick up a premium audio guide or simply soak in the Modernista streetscape at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the evening with cocktails at the rooftop bar of the Mandarin Oriental Barcelona on Passeig de Gràcia, offering sweeping city views. Dinner at Disfrutar (three Michelin stars) — book the premium tasting menu for a theatrical, avant-garde dining experience that defines contemporary Barcelona cuisine.

meals.lunch: Light bite at the hotel upon arrival or grab a gourmet sandwich and fresh juice at Federal Café on Carrer del Parlament, a short walk from Eixample
meals.dinner: Disfrutar — Michelin three-star restaurant on Carrer de Villarroel; reserve the Gran Menú Disfrutar tasting menu with optional wine pairing

Afterward, wander the charming Gràcia neighborhood — browse independent boutiques and admire the village-like plazas.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to refresh. Head to the rooftop bar at Hotel 1898 or the sky terrace at Ohla Eixample for pre-dinner Cava and city views. Dinner at Lasarte (three Michelin stars, Chef Martín Berasategui) on Carrer de Mallorca — an architectural gem of a dining room serving refined Basque-Catalan haute cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel's in-house restaurant or a premium spread at Parking Pizza's morning sibling, Brunch & Cake on Carrer d'Enric Granados (a pedestrian boulevard perfect for a morning coffee stroll)
meals.lunch: La Pepita in Gràcia — a beautifully tiled, design-forward spot serving elevated bocadillos and seasonal small plates; ideal after Park Güell
meals.dinner: Lasarte — Carrer de Mallorca 259; opt for the full tasting menu with Basque wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tower access well in advance as slots sell out quickly. Park Güell Monumental Zone requires timed tickets — purchase online before the trip. Gràcia is walkable from Park Güell and makes for a relaxed afternoon wind-down.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour — Embark on a private guided walk through Barcelona's medieval heart. Discover Roman ruins beneath the city streets, the magnificent Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, the ancient Jewish Quarter (El Call), and hidden courtyards. A knowledgeable private guide brings 2,000 years of layered history vividly to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tapas & Vermouth Food Tour in El Born — Transition seamlessly from the Gothic Quarter into the adjacent El Born district for a guided tapas and vermouth experience. Visit artisan vermouth bars, taste jamón ibérico de bellota, Catalan cheeses, fresh anchovies, and patatas bravas at curated stops. Explore the stunning El Born Cultural Centre (built over a 1714 archaeological site) between tastings.
day_by_day.evening: Nightlife Experience on Passeig del Born & Barceloneta Club Strip — Start the night with craft cocktails at a rooftop bar in El Born (Terraza del Liceu or Bar Calders). meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Espai Mescladís on Carrer dels Carders — a social enterprise café with outstanding pastries and single-origin coffee in El Born
meals.lunch: Included as part of the Tapas & Vermouth Food Tour — multiple premium stops across El Born covering a full, indulgent midday spread
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda or a light dinner of oysters and Cava at El Xampanyet (Carrer de Montcada) before the nightlife circuit begins — keep it light to pace the evening

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes for the morning Gothic Quarter walk — cobblestones are uneven. Book VIP table or bottle service at Pacha or Opium in advance, especially for a Saturday or peak August night. Barcelona nightlife starts late — clubs don't fill until after midnight.

day_by_day.morning: Late, leisurely morning to recover from the previous night. Enjoy a premium hotel breakfast in bed or at the hotel terrace. Mid-morning visit to the Fundació Antoni Tàpies on Carrer d'Aragó (a short walk from Eixample) — housed in a stunning Modernista publishing house, it showcases the work of Catalonia's greatest 20th-century artist alongside rotating contemporary exhibitions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private architectural tour of Eixample's Modernista gems — engage a specialist guide for a curated 3-hour deep dive into the Eixample grid's finest buildings: Palau del Baró de Quadras, Casa Terrades (Casa de les Punxes), and the interior of Casa Lleó Morera. Cap the afternoon with a visit inside Casa Batlló for the premium 'Magic Nights' or daytime immersive experience with augmented reality.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the rooftop of the El Palace Hotel (Gran Via de les Corts Catalanes) — one of Barcelona's most glamorous historic hotels. Dinner at Enigma by Albert Adrià — a cutting-edge, reservation-only restaurant offering a multi-sensory tasting journey through avant-garde Catalan cuisine across multiple atmospheric rooms.

meals.breakfast: Full luxury spread at the hotel — request room service with fresh-squeezed orange juice, pa amb tomàquet, local charcuterie, and pastries
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — a Barcelona institution for upscale tapas and fresh seafood; expect a queue but worth it, or book ahead
meals.dinner: Enigma by Albert Adrià — Carrer del Sepulcre 38; the full experiential tasting menu is mandatory and unforgettable; reserve months in advance

day_by_day.notes: Casa Batlló's immersive experience is best booked for the late afternoon slot to catch the light on the façade at golden hour. Enigma requires advance reservation and operates on a strict tasting-menu-only format — confirm dietary restrictions when booking.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning stroll along the elegant Passeig de Gràcia for last-minute luxury shopping — visit Loewe's flagship Modernista store inside Casa Loewe, or browse Custo Barcelona and local design boutiques. Stop for a final world-class coffee and croissant at Forn de Sant Jaume on Rambla de Catalunya.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from the hotel (arrange late check-out if possible — typically available with premium stays). Enjoy a farewell lunch at Moments (two Michelin stars) inside the Mandarin Oriental — Chef Raül Balam's refined take on Catalan grandmother recipes elevated to haute cuisine. Afterward, private luxury transfer to El Prat Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — no activities scheduled. Relax in the airport lounge before your onward flight.

meals.breakfast: Forn de Sant Jaume on Rambla de Catalunya — freshly baked croissants, ensaïmades, and premium coffee in a beautiful Belle Époque pastry shop
meals.lunch: Moments Restaurant, Mandarin Oriental Barcelona — Passeig de Gràcia 38–40; two Michelin stars; the Catalan tasting menu is a perfect farewell to the city's culinary identity
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight (no restaurant reservation needed)

day_by_day.notes: Request a late check-out (2:00–3:00 PM) from the hotel when booking to maximize the final morning without rushing. Confirm private transfer timing based on your return flight schedule — allow at least 2.5 hours before departure from El Prat. Forn de Sant Jaume opens early and is ideal for a relaxed final morning.
